text:
Predicates:
CanRegister(x) ::: x can register to vote in the United States.
ParticipatesInElection(x) ::: x participates in the 2024 United States presidential election.
HasCitizenship(x, y) ::: x has citizenship y.
RussianFederationOfficial(x) ::: x is a Russian Federation official.
Manager(x, y) ::: x is a manager at y.
Türk(x) ::: x has Turkish citizenship.
Vladimir ::: the individual Vladimir.
Ekaterina ::: the individual Ekaterina.
Premises:
∀x (CanRegister(x) → ParticipatesInElection(x)) ::: Everyone who can register to vote in the United States can participate in the election.
∀x (HasCitizenship(x, usa) → CanRegister(x)) ::: If someone has US citizenship, then they can register to vote.
(HasCitizenship(Vladimir, turk) ∨ HasCitizenship(Vladimir, russian)) ::: Vladimir has Turkish or Russian citizenship.
¬HasCitizenship(Vladimir, russian) ∧ ¬Manager(Vladimir, gazprom) ::: Vladimir neither holds Russian citizenship nor is he a manager at Gazprom.
(∃x (CanRegister(x) ∨ ParticipatesInElection(x))) ::: (Implied, based on the context)
Conclusion:
¬RussianFederationOfficial(Vladimir) ::: Vladimir is not a Russian Federation official.
